shipped_row.boundary_rationale: The address shifts from second-person rebuke to a third-person catalog of God's cosmic power: the departed spirits beneath the waters (web:Job.26.5; הָרְפָאִ֥ים יְחוֹלָ֑לוּ מִתַּ֥חַת מַ֝֗יִם וְשֹׁכְנֵיהֶֽם, oshb:Job.26.5), Sheol and Abaddon uncovered before him (web:Job.26.6; עָר֣וֹם שְׁא֣וֹל נֶגְדּ֑וֹ וְאֵ֥ין כְּ֝ס֗וּת לָֽאֲבַדּֽוֹן, oshb:Job.26.6), the sea stirred by his power and Rahab struck through by his understanding (web:Job.26.12; בְּ֭כֹחוֹ רָגַ֣ע הַיָּ֑ם ובתובנתו וּ֝בִתְבוּנָת֗וֹ מָ֣חַץ רָֽהַב, oshb:Job.26.12 -- a ketiv/qere pair sits inside this verse, single-witness disclosure), then the heavens garnished and his hand piercing the fleeing serpent (web:Job.26.13; בְּ֭רוּחוֹ שָׁמַ֣יִם שִׁפְרָ֑ה חֹֽלֲלָ֥ה יָ֝ד֗וֹ נָחָ֥שׁ בָּרִֽיחַ, oshb:Job.26.13). The catalog closes on a gnomic reflection: “Behold, these are but the outskirts of his ways. How small a whisper do we hear of him! But the thunder of his power who can understand?” (web:Job.26.14; הֶן אֵ֤לֶּה קְצ֬וֹת... מִ֣י יִתְבּוֹנָֽן, oshb:Job.26.14). Two further ketiv/qere pairs (his way/his ways; his power/his mighty acts) sit inside this closing verse (single-witness disclosure: oshb:Job.26.14), and a SAMEKH mark follows it in the same inventory (oshb:Job.26.14 (setumah, single-witness)). This row out-argues the very dominion doxology Bildad opened with at web:Job.25.2-Job.25.3, at five times the length.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Attributing this cosmological catalog to Bildad's developing argument rather than to Job's ironic escalation of it.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: God's cosmological power catalog ending whisper-saying

prev_row.boundary_rationale: Job's reply opens with the vaya'an formula, וַיַּ֥עַן אִיּ֗וֹב וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.26.1) -- the MT frame this row and the rest of the part follow through the third-cycle disarray of chapters 25-28. A PE mark precedes this opening, following Bildad's own close at Job.25.6 (oshb:Job.25.6 (petuchah, single-witness)). What follows is direct, second-person sarcasm aimed at Bildad: “How have you helped him who is without power! How have you saved the arm that has no strength!” (web:Job.26.2; מֶה עָזַ֥רְתָּ לְלֹא כֹ֑חַ ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ זְר֣וֹעַ לֹא עֹֽז, oshb:Job.26.2) and “To whom have you uttered words? Whose spirit came out of you?” (web:Job.26.4; אֶת מִ֭י הִגַּ֣דְתָּ מִלִּ֑ין וְנִשְׁמַת מִ֝י יָצְאָ֥ה מִמֶּֽךָּ, oshb:Job.26.4). The finite verbs addressed to Bildad in Job.26.2-Job.26.4a are second-person (עָזַ֥רְתָּ, ה֝וֹשַׁ֗עְתָּ, יָּ֭עַצְתָּ, הוֹדָֽעְתָּ, הִגַּ֣דְתָּ); the frame verbs of Job.26.1 are third-person wayyiqtols, and the relative clause of Job.26.4b (יָצְאָ֥ה, agreeing with its interrogative subject) is third-person feminine, with just the trailing מִמֶּֽךָּ carrying second person. The direct address to Bildad ends at Job.26.4, before the person shift to third-person cosmology at Job.26.5.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Extending Job's direct rebuke of Bildad through verse 14 instead of marking a shift at the person change to third-person cosmology at Job.26.5.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Job's sarcastic rebuke addressing Bildad directly

next_row.boundary_rationale: Job's mashal resumption opens with the vayosef formula, וַיֹּ֣סֶף אִ֭יּוֹב שְׂאֵ֥ת מְשָׁל֗וֹ וַיֹּאמַֽר (oshb:Job.27.1) -- the same wording, byte-for-byte, that reopens at web:Job.29.1 after the wisdom poem (sweep: 2 book-wide for this exact formula, byte tier: oshb:Job.27.1, oshb:Job.29.1), and per the MT frame this span governs everything through the end of chapter 28. The formula opens an oath of personal integrity: “As God lives, who has taken away my right, the Almighty, who has made my soul bitter” (web:Job.27.2; חַי אֵ֭ל הֵסִ֣יר מִשְׁפָּטִ֑י וְ֝שַׁדַּ֗י הֵמַ֥ר נַפְשִֽׁי, oshb:Job.27.2), closing “Far be it from me that I should justify you. Until I die I will not put away my integrity from me” (web:Job.27.5; חָלִ֣ילָה לִּי֮ אִם אַצְדִּ֪יק אֶ֫תְכֶ֥ם..., oshb:Job.27.5). Chapter 27 itself carries no PE or SAMEKH mark in the single-witness inventory -- a SAMEKH mark precedes this row's own opening, following Job.26.14 (setumah, single-witness), the mark closing the preceding cosmological catalog immediately before this oath begins -- so this row's internal edges rest on the formula and the oath's own asseverative particles rather than on mark corroboration.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Splitting the oath at the parenthetical aside in verse 3 instead of reading 27:1-6 as one continuous asseveration.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Job's self-imprecatory oath of personal integrity

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A deictic heading opens the row's final movement: “This is the portion of a wicked man with God, the heritage of oppressors, which they receive from the Almighty” (web:Job.27.13; זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק אָדָ֖ם רָשָׁ֥ע עִם אֵ֑ל וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת עָ֝רִיצִ֗ים מִשַּׁדַּ֥י יִקָּֽחוּ, oshb:Job.27.13) -- a verse carrying two paseq segs in the single-witness seg layer (oshb:Job.27.13 (paseq, single-witness)). The two-word deictic opening זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק is byte-identical to the closing verse of Zophar's second speech, oshb:Job.20.29 (זֶ֤ה חֵֽלֶק אָדָ֣ם רָ֭שָׁע מֵאֱלֹהִ֑ים וְנַחֲלַ֖ת אִמְר֣וֹ מֵאֵֽל, web:Job.20.29 “This is the portion of a wicked man from God, the heritage appointed to him by God”) -- sweep: 2 book-wide at byte tier, the object's only two members -- and the parallel continues into the second colon, where both verses open with וְֽנַחֲלַ֥ת (skeleton sweep: 3 book-wide, adding Job.31.2). What follows catalogs that wicked man's ruin -- children, wealth, house, and life all swept away -- closing “Men will clap their hands at him, and will hiss him out of his place” (web:Job.27.23; יִשְׂפֹּ֣ק עָלֵ֣ימוֹ כַפֵּ֑ימוֹ וְיִשְׁרֹ֥ק עָ֝לָ֗יו מִמְּקֹמֽוֹ, oshb:Job.27.23). The register here is close to the wicked-man's-doom catalog Zophar built his second speech around, and the byte-twinned heading strengthens that reading as more than a loose thematic echo; yet the MT text carries no new speech formula at this seam -- the material stays inside Job's vayosef mashal from web:Job.27.1 rather than being reassigned to a friend.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating verses 13-23 as displaced Zophar material and re-attributing them outside the vayosef frame.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Wicked man's comprehensive ruin from wealth grave

What follows argues wisdom's price is beyond purchase: “It can't be gotten for gold, neither will silver be weighed for its price” (web:Job.28.15; לֹא יֻתַּ֣ן סְג֣וֹר תַּחְתֶּ֑יהָ..., oshb:Job.28.15), running through onyx, sapphire, coral, crystal, and topaz before closing “The topaz of Ethiopia will not equal it. It won't be valued with pure gold” (web:Job.28.19). A PE mark follows in the single-witness inventory (oshb:Job.28.19 (petuchah, single-witness)), immediately before the refrain's second occurrence reopens the question in the row that follows (oshb:Job.28.20); another PE mark already precedes this row's own opening, following Job.28.11 (petuchah, single-witness), the mark closing the preceding mining excursus immediately before this price catalog begins.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: Confidence 'low' is honestly earned and the row's stated reason is its real weakness. Both edges are ruled tier-1 and clean: the span opens on the verse-initial protasis particle at oshb:Job.31.24 אִם שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י (WEB: If I have made gold my hope, web:Job.31.24), immediately after the preceding row's apodosis-curse and motive clause (web:Job.31.22, web:Job.31.23), and closes before the next verse-initial protasis at oshb:Job.31.29 אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י (web:Job.31.29). What the row cannot settle is internal, not edge-level: re-swept over verse_map_oshb.json, the span carries exactly three verse-initial particle tokens (oshb:Job.31.24; oshb:Job.31.25 אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י; oshb:Job.31.26 אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר) against a single apodosis at oshb:Job.31.28 גַּם ה֭וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י, and the row argues AGAINST the reading it holds (the additive particle opening Job.31.28 'most directly continues from the astral material immediately before it'), a rival that would split the span at Job.31.25|Job.31.26. A row that states the stronger rival and still holds belongs at the bottom of the band. The band is not masking a byte-defective warrant: every Hebrew run in the row collates at byte tier and every curly-quoted WEB run is verbatim (mechanical re-check of the shipped row in private scratch: 0 fixed / 0 defects; WEB quotes GREEN), and no ketiv/qere falls inside Job.31.24-Job.31.28. Under-statement is not indicated either, since a live internal split is a real cost. The two field defects recorded below are independent of the confidence band.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: אִם שַׂ֣מְתִּי זָהָ֣ב כִּסְלִ֑י ..., “If I have made gold my hope, and have said to the fine gold, ‘You are my confidence;’” (web:Job.31.24), opens a materialism sequence containing three independently verse-initial protases, not two: trust in gold (Job.31.24), a further wealth-increase clause (Job.31.25, אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח כִּי רַ֣ב חֵילִ֑י..., “If I have rejoiced because my wealth was great” web:Job.31.25), and astral reverence for sun and moon (Job.31.26, אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֖וֹר כִּ֣י יָהֵ֑ל ...וְ֝יָרֵ֗חַ יָקָ֥ר הֹלֵֽךְ, “if I have seen the sun when it shined, or the moon moving in splendor,” web:Job.31.26). One apodosis follows at Job.31.28 (גַּם ה֭וּא עָוֺ֣ן פְּלִילִ֑י, “this also would be an iniquity to be punished by the judges, for I would have denied the God who is above” web:Job.31.28), the verdict-formula עון פלילי that elsewhere at Job.31.11 closes one oath immediately preceding it (protasis Job.31.9, apodosis Job.31.10) rather than binding several protases together; the additive גַּם that opens Job.31.28 most directly continues from the astral material immediately before it (Job.31.26-Job.31.27) rather than reaching back to bind the wealth protases of Job.31.24-Job.31.25 into the same apodosis. That reading is disclosed as a live rival, not adopted: the row is chunked as written, with all three protases and the one following apodosis held inside its own span.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: A plausible alternative treats wealth (Job.31.24-Job.31.25) and celestial worship (Job.31.26-Job.31.28) as two separate oaths, each with its own protasis clauses; the verdict-formula parallel with Job.31.11 (skeleton sweep of עון פלילי: 2 book-wide, Job.31.11 and Job.31.28) is disclosed as corroboration for reading Job.31.28's apodosis as answering the immediately preceding astral protasis specifically, rather than as one warrant spanning all three protases of this row, without redrawing the row's own frozen edges.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Oath against malicious joy when foes destroyed

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The chapter's longest oath opens here, אִם אֶ֭מְנַע מֵחֵ֣פֶץ דַּלִּ֑ים ..., “If I have withheld the poor from their desire, or have caused the eyes of the widow to fail” (web:Job.31.16), and gathers four protasis clauses on compassion for the vulnerable -- Job.31.16, Job.31.19 (אִם אֶרְאֶ֣ה א֭וֹבֵד מִבְּלִ֣י ..., “if I have seen any perish for want of clothing, or that the needy had no covering” web:Job.31.19), Job.31.20 (a further 'if not' clause on warming the needy with fleece), and Job.31.21 (אִם הֲנִיפ֣וֹתִי עַל יָת֣וֹם ..., 'if I have lifted up my hand against the fatherless') -- before one shared apodosis-curse at Job.31.22 (כְּ֭תֵפִי מִשִּׁכְמָ֣ה תִפּ֑וֹל ..., 'then let my shoulder fall from the shoulder blade', web:Job.31.22) and its motive clause at Job.31.23. All four protases fall inside this span, none straddling its edges.
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Each of the four protases could in principle open its own row, but they share one topic, one apodosis, and one motive clause, so treating any one of these protasis tokens inside the cluster as a row boundary would cut a syntactically unified oath in pieces.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Oath against gold's seduction and wealth-worship idolatry

next_row.boundary_rationale: Three further protases follow in sequence without a change of apodosis pattern: rejoicing at an enemy's ruin, אִם אֶ֭שְׂמַח בְּפִ֣יד מְשַׂנְאִ֑י ..., “If I have rejoiced at the destruction of him” (web:Job.31.29); a hospitality claim introduced by the 'if not' idiom, אִם לֹ֣א ..., at Job.31.31; and concealment of sin at Job.31.33, אִם כִּסִּ֣יתִי כְאָדָ֣ם פְּשָׁעָ֑י ..., “if like Adam I have covered my transgressions, by hiding my iniquity in my heart” (web:Job.31.33). The prefixed form כְאָדָ֣ם is anarthrous -- equally 'like a human being' and 'like Adam' on the bytes alone; the named-figure reading follows the WEB's own choice rather than an article-marked or otherwise disambiguated Hebrew form. The prefixed form itself is a genuine skeleton-tier singleton (sweep: 1 book-wide, Job.31.33); the bare lexeme אדם behind it sweeps 28 book-wide at skeleton tier and is not usable without disambiguation, since it also catches a same-consonant false positive inside this very row's own span at Job.31.34's וָ֝אֶדֹּ֗ם ('I kept silence', root D-M-M ('to be silent'), unrelated to אדם). The row closes on the fear-of-exposure statement at Job.31.34 ('so that I kept silence, and didn't go out of the door'), just before the broken-off appeal that opens Job.31.35.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: The three topics (an enemy's downfall, hospitality, hidden sin) differ enough that three separate rows are defensible, but none of the intervening protasis clauses is answered by its own apodosis-curse the way the earlier oaths are, so the material is held together as one closing movement before the signature appeal.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Oath against stranger-deception and inhospitality fraud

queue_items.claim: The row labels the chapter's 17-token particle series a 'protasis series' and draws its ordinals from that count, an object conflation the book's own ruling forbids and the adjacent row rejects.
queue_items.grounds: Re-swept over verse_map_oshb.json (word-token search over the maqaf-free extract): the protasis particle stands in exactly 17 verses of Job 31 and is verse-initial in every one - Job.31.5, 31.7, 31.9, 31.13, 31.16, 31.19, 31.20, 31.21, 31.24, 31.25, 31.26, 31.29, 31.31, 31.33, 31.36, 31.38, 31.39. So '17', 'verse-initial' and the range Job.31.5 through Job.31.39 are TRUE, and Job.31.38 is the 16th and Job.31.39 the 17th TOKEN. But book LAW section 2e-b (ruling OL-c16) fixes the 17 as a PARTICLE-TOKEN count and excludes Job.31.36 אִם לֹ֣א עַל שִׁ֭כְמִי אֶשָּׂאֶ֑נּוּ (WEB: Surely I would carry it on my shoulder, web:Job.31.36) as an oath affirmation rather than a protasis, stating that protasis-clause counts are a different object. At the protasis object the series has 16 members, and oshb:Job.31.38 אִם עָ֭לַי is the 15th while oshb:Job.31.39 אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ is the 16th - so 'the sixteenth' and 'the series' true seventeenth and closing member' are false under the label the row itself applies. The conflation also puts the row at odds with its own immediate predecessor: M8-Job-127 (span Job.31.35-Job.31.37) applies OL-c16 in its own prose, calling the Job.31.36 particle an oath-affirmation idiom answering the wish rather than opening a further self-curse. Not alone load-bearing: the opening seam rests on the verse-initial particle standing in oshb:Job.31.38's own bytes, byte-true independent of any ordinal.
queue_items.proposed_change: Field repair only: name the object as the chapter's 17 verse-initial PARTICLE tokens (Job.31.5-Job.31.39) and either restate the ordinals at that object ('the sixteenth particle token') or give protasis-object ordinals with Job.31.36 excluded per LAW section 2e-b (Job.31.38 = 15th, Job.31.39 = 16th of 16). No span, seam or confidence change.

trigger_dispositions.grounds: The low band is honest and its stated reason is the real one. Book LAW section 8 names this material - the final protasis pair returning after the Job.31.35-Job.31.37 signature plea - as crux region 8, and rules that it be argued from the im-series positions rather than from emendation, which is what the row does ('the argument against moving it rests on what the substrate actually carries'). The closing edge is in fact the strongest in the book: the colophon תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב (WEB: The words of Job are ended. web:Job.31.40) stands in oshb:Job.31.40's own bytes and re-sweeps as a book-wide singleton (1 verse), with PE following that verse in the staged marks inventory (correctly typed petuchah, never conflated with setumah, single-witness disclosed, mark-follows-its-verse respected) - so the band is if anything conservative, and the genuinely contested edge is the opening one, which the row says. Nothing byte-false is sheltered by the label: the apodosis-sharing claim re-derives true (oshb:Job.31.40 opens with the briers-and-stinkweed curse and oshb:Job.31.39 אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ carries no apodosis of its own), all Hebrew runs collate at byte tier and all curly-quoted WEB runs are verbatim (0 fixed / 0 defects; WEB GREEN), and the marks inventory shows no ketiv/qere inside Job.31.38-Job.31.40, matching the row's own statement. The count-object and count-unit defects recorded below are field claims about the series and the apparatus, not artifacts of the confidence band.

shipped_row.boundary_rationale: A final protasis returns after the signature plea: אִם עָ֭לַי אַדְמָתִ֣י תִזְעָ֑ק ..., “If my land cries out against me, and its furrows weep together;” (web:Job.31.38), the sixteenth of the chapter's 17-token protasis series (verse-initial skeleton sweep, Job.31.5 through Job.31.39). A second, coordinate land-stewardship protasis follows in the same row's own span at Job.31.39 (אִם כֹּ֭חָהּ אָכַ֣לְתִּי בְלִי כָ֑סֶף וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלֶ֣יהָ הִפָּֽחְתִּי, “if I have eaten its fruits without money, or have caused its owners to lose their life” web:Job.31.39) -- the series' true seventeenth and closing member, sharing Job.31.38's apodosis-curse at Job.31.40a (“let briers grow instead of wheat, and stinkweed instead of barley”) rather than opening one of its own. The narrator's colophon follows in the same verse, תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב, “The words of Job are ended.” (web:Job.31.40) -- a construction swept as a book-wide singleton (sweep: 1 book-wide) -- closing Job's speech before the narrator's prose resumes: “So these three men ceased to answer Job, because he was righteous in his own eyes.” (web:Job.32.1). A petuchah follows Job.31.40 (oshb:Job.31.40 (petuchah, single-witness)), and the genre itself turns from verse to third-person prose at Job.32.1, doubling the colophon's own textual claim to end Job's words here.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: This final protasis pair has sometimes been read as displaced from its rhetorical position after the Job.31.35-Job.31.37 signature plea; the argument against moving it rests on what the substrate actually carries -- the colophon at Job.31.40 and the petuchah following it (oshb:Job.31.40 (petuchah, single-witness)) fix the sequence in place as written -- rather than on a claim about a manuscript-variant apparatus not attested in this chapter (its ketiv/qere occurrences number 2 -- Job.31.11 and Job.31.20 -- neither inside Job.31.38-Job.31.40). The row chunks the Masoretic sequence as it stands rather than adopting a rearrangement.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Job's field-oath closing final defense with tears

prev_row.boundary_rationale: The oath series breaks off for the signature plea: מִ֤י יִתֶּן לִ֨י שֹׁ֘מֵ֤עַֽ ..., “oh that I had one to hear me! Behold, here is my signature” (web:Job.31.35), a member of the two-word wish idiom מִ֤י יִתֶּן swept 9 verses book-wide at skeleton/consonantal tier (the pointed forms disagree across members: Job.11.5 reads יִתֵּ֣ן and Job.31.31 reads יִתֵּ֥ן, both against this verse's own יִתֶּן). Two of those nine are embedded, not the speaker's own wish: Job.31.31 sits inside a quoted household saying, and Job.11.5's יִתֵּ֣ן sits inside Zophar's speech (Job.11.1-Job.11.20, opened by וַ֭יַּעַן צֹפַ֥ר הַֽנַּעֲמָתִ֗י וַיֹּאמַֽר), not Job's -- the idiom is dialogue-wide, and both embedded members are disclosed here, not merely one of the two. Paseq falls in the OSHB seg layer at both Job.31.34 and Job.31.35 (oshb:Job.31.34 (paseq, single-witness); oshb:Job.31.35 (paseq, single-witness)), texture corroboration at the break. The protasis particle recurs once more inside this row at Job.31.36 (אִם לֹ֣א עַל ...), but here as an oath-affirmation idiom ('surely') answering the wish rather than opening a further self-curse, closing the row on Job.31.37's vow to approach God 'like a prince.'
prev_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Some would keep Job.31.35-Job.31.37 attached to the concealment oath just before it as its climax rather than a separate unit, but the wish-formula is a topic-turn interrogative-class marker distinct from every protasis clause around it, and no apodosis-curse connects Job.31.34 to what follows.
prev_row.literature_type_guess: Wish-formula calling God to give written indictment

next_row.boundary_rationale: The narrator closes out the three-cycle dialogue with a verdict rather than a fourth speech formula: “these three men ceased to answer Job” (web:Job.32.1), giving the reason with the closing clause כִּ֤י ה֖וּא צַדִּ֣יק בְּעֵינָֽיו – “he was righteous in his own eyes” (web:Job.32.1, oshb:Job.32.1). The sentence follows immediately on the colophon תַּ֝֗מּוּ דִּבְרֵ֥י אִיּֽוֹב "the words of Job are ended" (oshb:Job.31.40), a superscription/colophon-class boundary that belongs to the adjacent part; oshb:Job.32.1 (petuchah, single-witness) closes this verse on its own. The verse's grammatical subject, שְׁלֹ֤שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֣ים הָ֭אֵלֶּה “these three men,” settles the friends' role in the exchange before a new participant is named in the next verse, making this a self-contained narratorial beat rather than an opening clause of the Elihu introduction proper. The same two-word phrase closes the unit that follows, שְׁלֹ֥שֶׁת הָאֲנָשִׁ֗ים (oshb:Job.32.5) — a byte-true bracket running from this row's own verse (32:1) to that row's closing verse (32:5) (skeleton sweep: 2 book-wide, sole members 32:1 and 32:5) that argues continuity across the seam at 32:1|32:2 as much as it argues separation. What keeps 32:1 as its own row is the participant shift (Elihu named with a genealogy from 32:2) together with the double petuchah (32:1 and 32:5, both single-witness), not the phrase by itself.
next_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Folding this verse into the following Elihu-introduction row was considered and set aside, since its subject and verb belong to the friends' side of the account, not to Elihu's.
next_row.literature_type_guess: Three-friends' silence closing dialogue before Elihu

queue_items.claim: The 'pit' recurrence sentence names the wrong Hebrew tokens: it cites 33:18's מֵעֲבֹ֥ר and 33:22's נַפְשׁ֑וֹ as the bare and prefixed pit forms, when the pit tokens are 33:18 שָׁ֑חַת (bare) and 33:22 לַשַּׁ֣חַת (prefixed).
queue_items.grounds: The sweep arithmetic is exact: sweep.py --skel over the 'pit' skeleton שחת returns 7 VERSES book-wide - Job.9.31, Job.17.14, Job.33.18, Job.33.22, Job.33.24, Job.33.28, Job.33.30 - which is the row's member list verbatim. The two Hebrew tokens the sentence names, however, are not 'pit'. oshb:Job.33.18 word 6 is מֵעֲבֹ֥ר, the preposition-plus-infinitive rendered by WEB as "from perishing", and it carries a mem prefix, so it is not 'bare'; oshb:Job.33.22 word 3 is נַפְשׁ֑וֹ, "his soul", a suffixed form with no prefix, so it is not 'prefixed'. The actual 'pit' tokens are oshb:Job.33.18 word 4 שָׁ֑חַת (bare, etnachta) and oshb:Job.33.22 word 2 לַשַּׁ֣חַת (prefixed lamed with assimilated article, munach) - which is exactly the bare-versus-prefixed, not-pointed-identical contrast the sentence asserts, so the claim's substance is right and only the splices are wrong. Both mis-spliced runs are byte-valid substrings of the verses they are cited from, so the mechanical guard passes clean (normalize_hebrew_in_json.py over the shipped rows: 24 ok, 0 fixed, 0 defects): the error is semantic, the wrong-token-splice class. Load-bearing test: the sentence is texture DISCLOSED AND ARGUED AGAINST (it denies pointed identity across the seam), and the seam itself rests on the tier-1 scene shift standing in oshb:Job.33.19's bytes, וְהוּכַ֣ח בְּ֭מַכְאוֹב עַל מִשְׁכָּב֑וֹ, so the defect is not alone load-bearing -> medium, not high.
queue_items.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair only: replace "33:18's bare מֵעֲבֹ֥ר" with the bare pit token of oshb:Job.33.18, שָׁ֑חַת, and "33:22 carries its own prefixed form נַפְשׁ֑וֹ" with the prefixed pit token of oshb:Job.33.22, לַשַּׁ֣חַת, splicing both from verse_map_oshb.json rather than retyping. Span, seam, boundary_evidence_refs and confidence unchanged.

The next row opens a third illustration with its own protasis.
shipped_row.strongest_rejected_alternative: Treating this row as a continuation of the dream illustration before it was considered and rejected, since 33:19 opens a distinct affliction scene rather than extending the dream scene.
shipped_row.literature_type_guess: Sickness bringing nearness to death's appointed boundary

prev_row.boundary_rationale: A new scene opens the row, בַּחֲל֤וֹם חֶזְי֬וֹן לַ֗יְלָה – “In a dream, in a vision of the night” (web:Job.33.15, oshb:Job.33.15), the opening illustration of the thesis just stated at 33:14: in sleep, God opens the ear and warns (web:Job.33.16-33.17), and the row closes on the result, יַחְשֹׂ֣ךְ נַ֭פְשׁוֹ מִנִּי שָׁ֑חַת – “He keeps back his soul from the pit” (web:Job.33.18, oshb:Job.33.18). The next row opens a second illustration with a change of scene from dream to sickbed.
